findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` references `organization_context`, which is never defined in this method; additionally `OrganizationContext.member` is Optional/None for non-members and `has_global_access` is not an attribute of `OrganizationMember`. Because the line executes unconditionally before the `use_optimized` check, every request to the endpoint raises NameError/AttributeError, taking down audit log access for all users.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:837-839 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` is copied from `OffsetPaginator` (numeric keys) but the paginator is used with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a datetime; `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a datetime raises TypeError, crashing every optimized request with at least one result in `build_cursor` when the key is computed.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:841-842 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value (a millisecond-epoch string) instead of converting it back to a datetime the way `DateTimePaginator` does (`datetime.fromtimestamp(float(cursor.value)/1000)`); `build_queryset` then runs `filter(datetime__gt=<raw string>)`, which fails to parse (ValidationError → 500), so cursor-based navigation on the optimized path can never work.

[High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:876-881 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` relies on Django QuerySet slicing for negative bounds, which raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.`; the comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false, so the flagship negative-offset feature 500s on any negative-offset cursor and cannot work as designed.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184 — the shared `BasePaginator.get_result` used by every paginated endpoint was modified inconsistently: next-direction cursors with negative offsets are silently clamped to 0 (crafted cursors return page 1 with a 200 instead of erroring), while prev-direction cursors still pass the negative offset straight into `queryset[offset:stop]` and hit the same Django AssertionError; server-generated cursors never have negative offsets, so this only changes crafted-cursor behavior and only in one direction.

[Medium/security] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:176 / organization_auditlogs.py:70-71 — cursor offsets are fully client-controlled (`decode_cursor` accepts arbitrary integers from the base64 `cursor` query param) and are never validated; rather than rejecting negative offsets as invalid cursors, the PR adds multiple code paths intended to honor them. The superuser/global-access gate only guards the audit-log endpoint, while the `BasePaginator.get_result` change ships the new offset handling to every endpoint for every user, so the claimed 'authorized administrators' containment is not actually enforced by the code.

[Medium/performance] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator` constructs the identical queryset, applies the identical filters, and executes the identical `queryset[start:stop]` slice as `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator`; nothing reduces rows scanned, avoids counts, or changes query shape, so the PR delivers no measurable performance improvement and no benchmark supports the stated premise of the change.

[Medium/test_gap] No tests are added anywhere in the diff — nothing covers `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the `optimized_pagination` toggle, the admin gate, negative-offset cursors, or (most importantly given its blast radius) the `BasePaginator.get_result` change that alters slicing behavior for every paginated endpoint in the codebase.

[Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — the new `optimized_pagination` query parameter is undocumented (the endpoint docstring is not updated) and makes the same resource paginate with different semantics depending on the caller's role; cursors produced under `DateTimePaginator` are invalid under the optimized path and vice versa, so clients that toggle the flag or replay a cursor across modes get errors or inconsistent results.

[Medium/doc_defect] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:875,878 and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 — the comments make false safety claims that would mislead future maintainers into treating broken paths as validated: 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' (it raises AssertionError), 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' (org-level queryset scoping says nothing about offset validity), and the cursors.py comment implies a functional change enabling negative offsets where none exists (`int(offset)` always accepted negatives).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:841-842 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value (a millisecond-epoch string) instead of converting it back to a datetime the way `DateTimePaginator` does (`datetime.fromtimestamp(float(cursor.value)/1000)`); `build_queryset` then runs `filter(datetime__gt=<raw string>)`, which fails to parse (ValidationError → 500), so cursor-based navigation on the optimized path can never work.

adjudication.rationale: The optimized path in `organization_auditlogs.py` switches pagination to `OptimizedCursorPaginator` while still ordering by `-datetime`. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `get_item_key()` does `math.floor/ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`, which will be a `datetime` value for this endpoint, causing a type error (or otherwise incorrect cursor keying). Additionally, `value_from_cursor()` returns `cursor.value` without converting it back to a `datetime`, so `build_queryset(cursor_value, ...)` would receive a non-datetime cursor value for a datetime filter. Either way, cursor-based navigation on this optimized path is broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184 — the shared `BasePaginator.get_result` used by every paginated endpoint was modified inconsistently: next-direction cursors with negative offsets are silently clamped to 0 (crafted cursors return page 1 with a 200 instead of erroring), while prev-direction cursors still pass the negative offset straight into `queryset[offset:stop]` and hit the same Django AssertionError; server-generated cursors never have negative offsets, so this only changes crafted-cursor behavior and only in one direction.

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the new logic sets `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. This means negative offsets are clamped to 0 only for next-direction cursors, while prev-direction cursors still pass a negative start index into Django queryset slicing, which Django does not support (raises an AssertionError). This creates the inconsistent crafted-cursor behavior described (next returns page 1 instead of error/500; prev can still error). The diff also adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator` that explicitly allows negative slicing under `enable_advanced_features`, compounding the same issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:176 / organization_auditlogs.py:70-71 — cursor offsets are fully client-controlled (`decode_cursor` accepts arbitrary integers from the base64 `cursor` query param) and are never validated; rather than rejecting negative offsets as invalid cursors, the PR adds multiple code paths intended to honor them. The superuser/global-access gate only guards the audit-log endpoint, while the `BasePaginator.get_result` change ships the new offset handling to every endpoint for every user, so the claimed 'authorized administrators' containment is not actually enforced by the code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes cursor `offset` behavior more permissive without any validation. In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` (around line 176), the new logic clamps `offset` only when `not cursor.is_prev`, but for `cursor.is_prev` it uses `offset` directly (`start_offset = ... else offset`), meaning a negative `cursor.offset` from a client-controlled cursor can flow into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` for any endpoint using this paginator. Additionally, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` explicitly allows negative offsets when `enable_advanced_features` is set, again without validating the cursor origin or bounds. The audit-log endpoint gate (`use_optimized`/`enable_advanced`) only selects which paginator is used there; it does not prevent the global `BasePaginator.get_result` change from affecting other endpoints. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness/security exposure (client-controlled offsets influencing query slicing, potentially causing errors or unintended behavior) introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821 — `OptimizedCursorPaginator` constructs the identical queryset, applies the identical filters, and executes the identical `queryset[start:stop]` slice as `BasePaginator`/`DateTimePaginator`; nothing reduces rows scanned, avoids counts, or changes query shape, so the PR delivers no measurable performance improvement and no benchmark supports the stated premise of the change.

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` still builds a queryset via `self.build_queryset(...)` and ultimately executes a standard Django slice `queryset[start_offset:stop]` and materializes it with `list(...)`, just like the existing paginator logic shown earlier in the diff (`results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`). Aside from optional negative-offset handling and an extra flag, the query shape/row fetching pattern is essentially unchanged in the diff, and the PR contains no benchmarks or evidence supporting the claimed performance gains. This is a substantiated review concern but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No tests are added anywhere in the diff — nothing covers `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the `optimized_pagination` toggle, the admin gate, negative-offset cursors, or (most importantly given its blast radius) the `BasePaginator.get_result` change that alters slicing behavior for every paginated endpoint in the codebase.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic and changes behavior without adding any tests. Specifically: (1) `organization_auditlogs.py` introduces an `optimized_pagination` query toggle plus an admin gate (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`) and switches paginator class to the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` when enabled. (2) `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` modifies `BasePaginator.get_result` slicing by introducing `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which can affect pagination behavior across all endpoints using this paginator. (3) A brand-new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class is added with special negative-offset slicing behavior when `enable_advanced_features` is true. No test files or test changes appear anywhere in the diff to cover these new paths and the high-blast-radius base paginator change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — the new `optimized_pagination` query parameter is undocumented (the endpoint docstring is not updated) and makes the same resource paginate with different semantics depending on the caller's role; cursors produced under `DateTimePaginator` are invalid under the optimized path and vice versa, so clients that toggle the flag or replay a cursor across modes get errors or inconsistent results.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds an `optimized_pagination` query param and switches pagination implementation based on both that flag and caller privileges (`use_optimized` + `enable_advanced`), meaning the same endpoint can paginate with different semantics depending on role (organization_auditlogs.py). Nothing in the diff indicates cursors are made interoperable across `DateTimePaginator` vs `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (no mode marker in cursor, no translation), so a cursor obtained in one mode being reused in the other is plausibly incompatible. The claim about missing docstring updates is not verifiable from the shown diff, but the role/flag-dependent semantics issue is diff-grounded and actionable as an API design/backwards-compat concern rather than a definite functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/doc_defect] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:875,878 and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 — the comments make false safety claims that would mislead future maintainers into treating broken paths as validated: 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' (it raises AssertionError), 'This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' (org-level queryset scoping says nothing about offset validity), and the cursors.py comment implies a functional change enabling negative offsets where none exists (`int(offset)` always accepted negatives).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds comments asserting safety/behavior that isn’t demonstrated by the code change. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` the new branch explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when negative and claims “Django ORM properly handles negative slicing” and “This is safe because permissions are checked…”, but the diff itself provides no validation/guards for negative offsets beyond those comments. In `utils/cursors.py`, the new comment implies a functional change (“Allow negative offsets…”) even though `self.offset = int(offset)` already accepted negatives before; only the comment changed. These are misleading documentation claims rather than a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.
